question: Should context-padding-only static evidence for GitHub-backed skills stay as ClawScan input/reviewer context, or may it directly mark a clean-installable GitHub-backed skill as publicly suspicious?
rationale: Current main's spec and code make the worker-backed ClawScan result the GitHub-backed verdict boundary, and flagged.suspicious changes public visibility.

options.title: Keep As ClawScan Context
options.body: Require the PR to route the detector through the current prepare/chunk/finalize scan flow and avoid public suspicious state from static evidence alone.

options.title: Approve Public Suspicious State
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally let padding-only evidence hide clean-installable GitHub-backed skills, but that needs explicit policy, tests, and runtime proof.

options.title: Pause Security Direction
options.body: Keep the PR draft or close it until a maintainer-sponsored scan-boundary design is ready.

recommendation.title: Keep As ClawScan Context
recommendation.body: Require the PR to route the detector through the current prepare/chunk/finalize scan flow and avoid public suspicious state from static evidence alone.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the current GitHub-backed scan flow and authored the current spec invariant in the available history.
